items.title: Keshav Enterprises
items.subtitle: Intern · India
items.summary: Built the data and ML backbone for an SME manufacturer: an ELT pipeline replacing spreadsheet tracking, a RAG system for grounded customer replies, and an evaluation harness that decided which forecasting models were allowed to ship.
bullets: Architected an end-to-end ELT pipeline in Python and PostgreSQL, normalizing sales inquiry and order data across 4 relational entities to replace manual spreadsheet tracking for an SME manufacturer

Built a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline using ChromaDB vector search and the Claude API to auto-draft grounded customer replies, constraining outputs to retrieved catalog data to eliminate hallucinated pricing

Achieved a 49% relative MAPE reduction (52.0% → 26.6%) with Prophet on the one product line where sufficient trend signal existed, validating that the harness caught a genuine case for deployment

items.title: Change Assurance Runtime
items.subtitle: for AI Coding Agents · VT Hacks 14
items.summary: A local-first Windows runtime that puts AI coding agents under independent supervision: every process they spawn is attributed, every action is journaled in a tamper-evident log, and every change ships with a signed passport.
bullets: Built a local-first Windows runtime using kill-on-close Job Objects and restricted-token process launches to attribute every descendant process by PID, image path, and command line

Designed a tamper-evident, hash-chained event journal with end-to-end replay verification and a signed Ed25519 Change Passport capturing intent, authority, evidence, and outcomes for every agent action
Shipped three clients (Textual TUI, CLI, Electron/React desktop) against one frozen OpenAPI contract of 66 operations, 61 routes, and 110 typed schemas
Validated by a threat-model review (15 of 16 findings fixed) and 1,022 passing tests

items.title: Job Search Automation
items.subtitle: A zero-cost daily pipeline on GitHub Actions
items.summary: Finds fresh job postings every morning, scores them against my resume, drafts tailored bullets, compiles a PDF, logs everything to a tracking spreadsheet, and emails a summary, all on free infrastructure.
bullets: Discovers postings from public Greenhouse and Lever job-board APIs and other public boards on a GitHub Actions schedule, so there is no server to maintain
Scores each posting against the resume with the Gemini API and rewords the most relevant bullets for that role
Compiles a tailored LaTeX resume PDF, logs every posting to Google Sheets with an Eligibility column, and emails a morning summary
Backed by a test suite covering discovery quality, queueing, pipeline limits, and workflows

items.title: Regime Detection

Developed a transaction-cost-aware backtesting framework with filtered probability inference, benchmarked against K-Means and momentum strategies
Achieved a 57.97% return with ~34% lower volatility than Buy-and-Hold

items.title: Fork-Join Thread Pool
items.subtitle: Work-stealing task parallelism in C · CS 3214
items.summary: A fork/join framework for parallel divide-and-conquer algorithms, built up in stages from a single-lock work-sharing pool to a work-stealing pool with per-worker deques. Built with a partner.
bullets: Implemented a thread pool and futures API (submit, future_get, shutdown) in C with pthreads, evolving it from a single-lock work-sharing queue to per-worker deques with work stealing
Prevented deadlock with helping: a worker that joins a not-yet-started task executes it inline, while external threads wait instead of helping
Replaced the global lock with finer-grained per-worker locking, keeping each task's state change atomic with its removal from a queue so exactly one thread runs it
Kept idle workers blocked on condition variables (no busy-waiting), checked for data races with Helgrind, and benchmarked parallel speedup on 32-core Xeon machines

items.title: Minibash
items.subtitle: A bash-subset shell in C · CS 3214
items.summary: A command-language interpreter implementing a subset of bash: pipelines, redirection, variables, command substitution, and control flow, with every job running in its own process group. Built with a partner.
bullets: Built a shell in C that parses scripts with the Tree-sitter bash grammar and runs simple commands, pipelines, && / || lists, if/elif/else, and for/while loops with break
Launched processes with posix_spawnp instead of fork + exec, wiring pipes and file redirection (including |& and >&) through spawn file actions and giving each job its own process group
Implemented quoting, variable expansion ($?, $$, ${var}), and $(…) command substitution, matching bash's exit-status rules (last pipeline stage; 128 + signal number)
Tracked child processes via SIGCHLD and waitpid, and verified memory safety under Valgrind

items.title: Malloc Lab
items.subtitle: A 64-bit dynamic memory allocator in C · CS 3214
items.summary: My own malloc, free, and realloc: a 64-bit allocator tuned to balance space utilization against throughput on trace-driven benchmarks. Built with a partner.
bullets: Implemented mm_malloc, mm_free, and mm_realloc returning 16-byte-aligned blocks, going beyond the implicit-free-list baseline the assignment disallowed as a final design
Designed the heap block layout and free-block organization, with splitting and coalescing to limit fragmentation
Tuned against a performance index weighting space utilization (60%) and throughput (40%) using the course's trace-driven driver
Encapsulated pointer arithmetic in static helper functions and guarded invariants with assertions to keep untyped memory code debuggable
